My opinion is there isn't a sensor out there today that can get most any job done, sans high-end fashion type stuff where MF is king. Behind? Maybe, but they all leap-frog each other.

Sounds like you need something with better construction for wear and tear. That's legit. You'd probably benefit from an upgrade to a prosumer body that's not just all plastic. (magnesium, etc..). If wear and tear is a concern, I'd (in my opinion, just mine) recommend staying away from the current mirrorless systems out there. They aren't nearly as knock-around durable as the pro-sumer DSLR's.

Switching to another vendor like Nikon? Eh. I mean, if you can afford it, sure. You could probably consolidate your glass into 2 lenses at the pro end of the spectrum too. For Nikon, something like the 24-70 and the 70-200...and if you needed a fast prime the 50 1.8 is cheap. But that's a cost thing you'd have to weigh.

For those that don't know the Evil Dead series, this is the first of the original trilogy. The second one is basically a remake of the first one, but crazier (and better IMHO). The third one is a crazy cheese fest of one liners and bad puns (that's not a bad thing). Bruce Cambell was the breakout (cult) star in these.

A couple years ago they rebooted the Evil Dead, basically using the storyline of the first (and so, second) movie. It didn't go so well. No Bruce, either (besides a cameo).

Recently I read a headline about Ash vs The Evil Dead, with Bruce. It could have potential.

So, long story short, you could skip this one and watch the second and third and know what's up, but this one is good to start with just to see how it got it's start (and gives you something to compare the second to, so you can see how they did more craziness with the same story). It's also the most 'horror' horror movie out of them, I think. The others are closer to comedy-horror, except the reboot, I think that was pretty much straight horror.
Also that bit where Ash says "You bastards! Why are you torturing me like this!? WHY, WHY!?" is hilarious.
I remember walking down the video rental store and seeing the cover. Didn't rent it until years later.

For those that have seen Raimi's Evil Dead, I highly suggest you watch this movie - Equinox (1970) (note: it's not actually 2hr 40min, it's only half that, for some reason they doubled it up). Never knew this movie existed until about a month or two ago, watched it at a friends' as we were browsing around Prime or Netflix. And I just kept seeing parallels between it and 1981's Evil Dead.

Equinox has the isolated cabin in the woods, a group going there for a getaway, a monster that attacks it, a demonic book, control of a person by demon... and there are even some visuals. The trademark Raimi camera motion where the camera gives that view of the creature on the attack? Even THAT was taken from Equinox. As well as that scene from Army of Darkness with the book intro, it spiraling. That visual is taken from Equinox.

I honestly can't look at Raimi's "masterpiece" the same way ever again after stumbling upon this movie.
